question: Which tissue is specialised for transmitting rapid electrical impulses that enable muscle movement?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nervous tissue**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Nervous tissue** is specialized for transmitting **rapid electrical impulses**, which are essential for communication between different parts of the body.
 
• This tissue consists of **neurons** (nerve cells) and **supporting cells** (glial cells) that work together to process and transmit signals.
 
• Neurons have unique structures such as **axons** and **dendrites**, which enable them to carry signals over long distances and connect with other neurons or tissues like muscles.
 
• **Nervous tissue** plays a critical role in controlling muscle movement by transmitting signals from the brain to the muscles through the **central and peripheral nervous systems**.
 
• This tissue is found in the **brain, spinal cord, and peripheral nerves**, and is integral to the functioning of the body, including voluntary and involuntary responses.
